📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Koni De Winter spoke at an event at the AC Milan store today, and he covered numerous topics with a lot of openness.

It has been revealed that this season, De Winter has found himself in a new, important light. Matteo Gabbia spent most of pre-season in the middle of the back three, but injuries have prevented him from playing much of a role in the campaign.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s an unfortunate shame and there may have been some worries about De Winter taking on this role. However, he’s taken the opportunity in his stride, looking every part a starter in Ruben Amorim’s defence.

According to recent reports, rumours about a upcoming defender arriving will persist, so it’ll be interesting to see what happens with his minutes from January onwards. However, he’s created something of a headache, but it’s a good one to have.

Speaking to SportMediaset on the sidelines of the Meet&Greet at the Milan Store in San Babila, via MilanNews, De Winter looked at the rise in his playing time, Amorim’s closeness to the group and much more.

You also took over at Reggio Emilia when Gabbia was unfortunately injured. You’re practically always there; what does that mean to you?

“I’m playing a lot, it’s great to be playing. We’re playing a lot, and these days you train more on taking care of your body, keeping healthy, and right now I’m doing that more, but it’s great to be playing a lot of games. Playing a lot of games for Milan, and it’s even better to win games.”.

It’s all great, but it wasn’t a given: you’ve earned this place as leader. Do you now feel like a leader of this AC Milan?

It has been revealed that “I feel good at this Milan club, and as I always say, I try to give what I can. It’s also true that I might have a more vital position this year. That might be true, but I always try to do my part, give my all, and help my teammates.”.

It’s clear, evident, that Amorim holds you in high regard, but what is Amorim like? An adjective.

Sources indicate that “I’d say he’s very human. He’s one of us, he laughs, he has fun, but when he has to be serious, he’s serious. He lives with the group, the group feels close to him, and I think that gives the players a good feeling. It’s nice to work for him and with him.”.

Is it true that he got very angry after the defeat against Ferencvaros?

“Yes, but I think the whole group felt that we had played a very poor game, so, as I saw it, my teammates saw it too.”.

Are Ferencvaros and Bologna two games you’re ready to say “never again” to? Will Frosinone be a different team?

“Yes, exactly, as I stated, we are very confident, but sometimes even too much so, and then all matches are difficult against whoever we play against, and we have to understand this quickly and we can’t make the same mistakes.”.

Among the various critics, it’s said that this AC Milan team has enormous potential, but there are too many ups and downs. Does it need more consistency?

“Yes, I think it hurts even more when we lose because we know we can do well, we can win every game. So yes, when we really lose, in the locker room you feel like we’ve let ourselves down first and then everyone else.”.

You recently became the father of a beautiful baby girl. What are your nights like as a dad?

“At night, I’m fine. My girlfriend is working really hard, so it’s a lot for me. I mean, I get up sometimes, but it’s much quieter. I think it’s harder for her.”.

And how much has life changed with the arrival of a daughter?

“It’s changed a lot, I mean, I don’t know how to explain it. When you’re at work, you think about your daughter, you want to come home earlier, you want to hold her, you want her – I mean, you have more beautiful moments – but it’s hard to explain. I don’t know how to explain it.”.

You were also used as a full-back, but now you only play as a centre-back….

“Good, good, because I also consider myself a centre-back, but it’s true that I can also play full-back. It’s something I can do, but it’s not my favourite position. But yes, it’s true that I’ve played a few games there in the past, but I’m happy playing as a centre back and I’m happy that the coach sees that too.”.

In a recent development, “I mean, crazy in a good way, yes. He likes to have fun, he likes to dance, he likes to talk, so he’s a bright spot, as they say, for the locker room, yes.”.

“Well, that’s a good question. Yes, I miss her. I thought about it even when the little girl was born: I also want to score a goal, I mean, dedicate a goal to her, so I miss her, yes.”.

It has been revealed that how do you concentrate when you’re in the hotel retreat? How do you focus in the hours leading up to kick-off?

“It’s become a routine now, so I always do the same things. You’re in the hotel, you take a shower, you play a little video game or you’re on your phone, so now I don’t even think about it, it’s really become a routine.”.

What does Maignan ask of you, defenders?

“He says to stay focused on the game because, as we know, one moment can change the game and at Milan it can also change a season, so it’s very notable not to underestimate every moment and always stay focused.

It seems to me that there is a great understanding between you and Strahinja Pavlovic even off the pitch….

“Yes, it’s true, he and I have a good relationship; we met last year. Then when you see him you might not think, I mean, I didn’t think he would be such a great friend, but we got along really well both on and off the pitch, it’s really nice to spend time with him.”.

Recent findings suggest that our 007s at Milanello tell us about some great ping pong matches between you and Pavlovic. Who’s the better player?

According to recent reports, “This is difficult, but he started at a much higher level than me. But now I’ve improved a lot, although I have to say he’s even stronger. But yes, every day we start with a game of ping pong and then we start working.”.

Would you like your daughter to play soccer in the future? Are you planning a second child? Would you like to have a son who plays soccer?

“I want her to do what she wants, where she feels good, where she doesn’t feel pressured, and where she can express herself best. And then, going back to ping pong, I think there’s some video; maybe we can see me beat her.”.

Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

Recent findings suggest that if you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

According to recent reports, poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

In a recent development, “With Alex, it is clear,” stated Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

It has been revealed that A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his upcoming territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

In a recent development, quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Industry observers note that iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move confirmed the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

In a recent development, it was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still indicated great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Industry observers note that inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

Sources indicate that there will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

Sources indicate that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The notable thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

Industry observers note that “We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

In a recent development, “It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

In a recent development, we are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

Industry observers note that “We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola remarked. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

It has been revealed that “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

Sources indicate that “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

Rangers avoid title blip as late own goal breaks Motherwell resistance and Celtic kept within eyeline

  • With the contest seemingly bound to end 1-1, a potentially significant blip for the visitors in terms of their title aspirations, Ryan Naderi’s 88th-minute effort struck the unfortunate Martin Moormann and looped past goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, inflicting the cruellest of blows on the Steelmen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the crisp chill of a late November evening in North Lanarkshire, Rangers required a late deflection to prise three vital Scottish Premiership points from the grasp of a resolute and industrious Motherwell side.

With the contest seemingly bound to end 1-1, a potentially significant blip for the visitors in terms of their title aspirations, Ryan Naderi’s 88th-minute effort struck the unfortunate Martin Moormann and looped past goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, inflicting the cruellest of blows on the Steelmen.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

There seemed an almost ritualistic rhythm to Rangers’ recent visits to Fir Park: waves of possession crashing against a disciplined claret-and-amber breakwater, accompanied by the persistent nagging doubt that dominance without ruthlessness invites punishment.

Derek McInnes’s side were living out that exact cautionary tale on their latest visit before Naderi popped up with a crucial late winner.

For the opening 15 minutes, this contest threatened to become a procession. Rangers monopolised the ball and the opening goal arrived after just eight minutes. Motherwell’s defensive structure momentarily frayed under early pressure, allowing centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez to rise unmarked and head home Kim Min-Su’s corner with disarming simplicity.

According to recent reports, at that juncture, Motherwell appeared to be unravelling. Within six minutes of falling behind, Alfred Johansson was forced into an early reshuffle when winger Ibrahim Mentioned limped off injured in visible distress to be replaced by Regan Charles-Cook.

Rangers sensed blood. Naderi probed tirelessly, Djeidi Gassama repeatedly cut inside off the left flank to test the Steelmen defence, and Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was called upon to produce a string of top-class saves to prevent the visitors from establishing an unassailable cushion.

However, Scottish football rarely rewards aesthetic superiority alone. Having weathered the initial storm without conceding a second, the hosts summoned an equaliser from their first corner of the evening in the 21st minute. Emmanuel Longelo rolled a clever short pass to Tom Sparrow, whose curling delivery into the penalty area found Jake Girdwood-Reich entirely unmarked. The Australian defender needed no second invitation, sweeping a composed finish past Ivor Pandur to restore parity against the run of play.

Recent findings suggest that that subtly altered the psychological temperature inside Fir Park. While Rangers continued to dictate proceedings, racking up nearly 20 attempts on goal, their lack of cutting edge in the final third was glaring. Before the interval, Paulsen defied the visitors once more with a superb reflex stop from Nico Raskin in the 41st minute.

McInnes’ men pressed forward with renewed urgency after a stern half-time team talk. Seven minutes into the second half, Dan Neil drifted into a pocket of space on the edge of the area and drilled a low effort that whistled agonisingly past the post.

Visible frustration began to creep into Rangers’ ranks passing the hour mark as a combination of misplaced passes and poor finishing drew audible groans from the packed away end.

Sensing his team’s grip on the contest loosening, McInnes turned to his bench in the 69th minute, introducing summer signing Kevin Kelsy in place of Gassama to add a greater physical presence in attack alongside Naderi. There was little immediate improvement. Badredine Bouanani raced down the right flank and cut the ball back for Neil, whose shot sailed high and wide.

Motherwell were looking increasingly comfortable and Tawanda Maswanhise tested Pandur from distance as the home side sensed an opportunity to claim something more substantial than a point.

Findlay Curtis was introduced for Rangers and almost made an immediate impact, delivering an excellent cross towards the back post which Naderi was unable to turn home from close range.

Then came another extraordinary intervention from Paulsen. Curtis' effort appeared to have beaten the keeper, who could only palm the ball into the path of Sterling. However, Paulsen recovered magnificently to divert the right-back’s follow-up onto the crossbar. It was a remarkable piece of goalkeeping and, by this stage, it seemed entirely possible that the home side would clinch a share of the spoils.

They were not to be so fortunate.

With two minutes remaining, Rangers finally found the breakthrough their territorial dominance had threatened to deliver. Naderi got his effort away, but Moormann intervened and inadvertently diverted the ball beyond his own goalkeeper. The unfortunate centre-back could do little about the decisive deflection, but the consequences were devastating for Motherwell.

The travelling Rangers support erupted, relief and celebration combining in equal measure. For McInnes, it was a precious late reward for a side that had made unnecessarily hard work of a match they might have settled long before the closing stages.

The victory extends Rangers' unbeaten run in all competitions to 13 matches and ensures they remain in touch with Celtic, moving back within four points of the league leaders with a game in hand.

But his ousting has drawn an angry reaction from many on social media, with some saying it is a ‘disgraceful’ decision.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

A statement issued by the club a couple of hours after the first reports on X that the decision had been made stated: “Eastbourne Town F.C have today parted manufacturer with First Team Manager Jude MacDonald and his coaching staff.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and his management team for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting new arrivals, just two years later debuted an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish runners-up and then win the league play-off final.

“They then successfully kept the club in the Isthmian FL for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

"The club wish them all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”.

Earlier in the day Town held Whitstable – third in the league – to a 0-0 draw at The Saffrons , a week after a 1-1 draw with Sheppey, who are also in the top half.

At the end of the Whitstable game, the club’s X account said: “A brilliant performance from The Town. A hard earned point and it could have been three after an excellent second half.”.

The news comes just a day after the club revealed the return to the club of James Stone and James Waters.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 17:30.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has talked up both Mike Penders and Emiliano Martinez ahead of Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

The Blues will be bidding to remain in the top five of the Premier League table when they host the Yorkshire giants at Stamford Bridge.

While Alonso has a number of injury challenges, which were addressed at Friday's press conference, he must also decide who to select between the sticks.

Martinez has been sidelined since the middle of October after suffering a fractured jaw at Everton.

Although Penders's inexperience highlighted on his first Premier League start versus Tottenham Hotspur, the Belgian has since impressed.

When quizzed on Martinez, Alonso suggested that the Argentina international was exactly where they wanted him to be nearly five weeks into his recovery.

He told reporters: "He's in the squad and he's selectable against Sunderland. It was two weeks ago, probably there was risk, but the plan was for him to train more with Argentina, to play one game.

"He remarked well, so he's available for tomorrow.".

Immediately after that question, Alonso was asked whether Penders was capable of becoming Chelsea's number one.

The Spaniard added: "Mike has done very good things.

"I think that we know the progression that he had, that he overcame a difficult moment for sure after the first game, but after he's done better, he's getting improving and with three minutes his development has been good.".

With his selection on Saturday, Alonso will reveal whether his preference is to pick players on form or reputation.

Against Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, Penders has arguably performed better than expectations.

Penders deserves to retain his place in the team, but Martinez was signed by Chelsea to be their number one.

Whoever finds themselves on the substitutes' bench will feel relatively hard done by.

Harry Kane is one of the main contenders for the prestigious Best Men's Player prize at the Globe Soccer Awards - and you can vote for the winner.

The Ballon d'Or king is joined by England team-mates Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, and Bukayo Saka in the category.

Meanwhile, Lionesses star Alessia Russo is the sole English representative in contention for the Best Women's Player honour.

Voting is now open across 12 categories, with the awards to be handed out at a glitzy ceremony in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on December 28.

The Globe Soccer Awards began in 2010 and have since become popular among fans worldwide, with more than 100 million votes cast in some years.

Last year's winner Ousmane Dembele is also in the running for Best Men's Player, with Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe joining him in the 26-strong shortlist.

Harry Kane, pictured with the Ballon d'Or, is among the nominees for Best Men's PLayer at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Voting is now open across 12 award categories ahead of a ceremony in Dubai in December.

Erling Haaland won the Best Men's Player prize for 2023 and is in contention again.

Premier League stars Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, William Saliba, and Dominik Szoboszlai are also hoping to get their hands on the prize.

Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery are in the running for Best Coach, while Myles Lewis-Skelly and Nico O'Reilly are competing for the Emerging Player gong.

There are 14 categories, with a 'Career and Special Awards' section yet to see its talent confirmed.

Arsenal are hopefuls in the Best Club category for both men and women, with Aston Villa joining them in the former and Manchester City in the latter.

There will also be prizes for the best forward, midfielder, defender, and goalkeeper, and Fans' Historic Club, Best Sporting Director, and Best Agent.

Ronaldo, a serial winner at the ceremony, is defending his Best Middle East Player crown after winning his first Saudi Pro League title with Al-Nassr. Ivan Toney is among his rivals for that.

Fans are able to cast their votes until November 30, after which a jury including the likes of Antonio Conte and Luis Figo will also have their say.

It is an event of truly global interest, with supporters from more than 225 countries having cast votes in previous editions.

'We are incredibly proud to return for our third consecutive year as title partner of the GLOBE SOCCER Awards,' noted Adil Taqi, CEO of title sponsor BEYOND Developments.

'Our continued partnership reflects BEYOND Developments’ commitment to connecting with an international audience through shared passions and experiences.

Sources indicate that 'Football brings people together across cultures and borders, resonating with our belief in pushing boundaries and aiming higher, a mindset shared by the players, coaches and clubs who will be honoured this December. When asked about his thought process around making that change to the formation, Blackwell mentioned: “Well we haven’t kept many clean sheets have we.”.

The result justified the extra body he added to the defence to sure it up at the back and he was full of praise for the way his side defended.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 17:31.

Chelsea will be looking to extend a 27-year streak when they play Leeds United.

The Blues head into Saturday's fixture at Stamford Bridge sitting in fifth place in the Premier League table.

However, Leeds make the trip to West London knowing that they will move ahead of their next opponents with a win.

Possessing a rivalry that has lasted decades, the encounter is highly anticipated, with Alonso having both injury concerns and selection dilemmas for this contest.

Nevertheless, the Spaniard will be encouraged by Chelsea's recent record versus the Yorkshire giants.

Leeds are making their second trip to Stamford Bridge this season, having already going down 6-3 to Chelsea in a chaotic EFL Cup tie in September.

That was the 10th match in succession that Chelsea have avoided defeat to Leeds at their home ground.

Chelsea have recorded eight wins and two draws during that period, with Leeds not prevailing since a Stephen McPhail double earned them a 2-0 victory in 1999.

Most notably, that triumph sent Leeds to the top of the Premier League table in December of that year.

Despite Chelsea's dominant Stamford Bridge record, Leeds avoided defeat to Chelsea in last season's Premier League.

Although, an Enzo Fernandez goal earned Chelsea a 1-0 success in the FA Cup semi-finals in 2026-27.

Leeds head into this fixture having recorded five points from their five away matches in this season's Premier League.

However, they have already played the top-two Arsenal and Brighton & Hove Albion on their travels, as well as Nottingham Forest, in-form Bournemouth and Sunderland.

Here are five things we learned.

In a recent development, there was a drastic change in formation as the Reds moved to a back three with Ben Heneghan in the middle of the back three with Josh Flint and Charlie Barker either side. Blackwell also decided to field an extra striker with Pemi Aderoju and Danilo Orsi leading the line.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Playing two strikers from the very start is something fans have been crying out for with it being a rarity this season for two strikers to start from the outset with the Reds typically bringing on a second striker towards the end of a game.

Industry observers note that it evidently paid off not just in terms of the result but the performance. Orsi is a player who needs service; he isn’t a target man and he isn’t someone whose strong suit is running in behind, so having Aderoju alongside him only compliments him and ultimately brings the best out of each other's game, especially if Crawley continue to play direct.

This win over Fleetwood is Crawley’s first home league since Colin Kazim-Richards first game in charge at the end of March, which was eight months ago.

To hang on to that lead at the end was crucial. Having not had a home league win this season, that would have played on the minds of the players and it was certainly felt in the crowd.

But to now overcome that hurdle, the Reds can really look to make the Broadfield Stadium a fortress going forward.

The Reds seemed to have a lot more fight with a real intensity to the way they played, an element of their game which Blackwell alluded to in his post-match interview also.

They had a lot of time to prepare for today’s game having had no game last weekend, and so that would have allowed not only more time to work on tactical elements of the game, but also their fitness and sharpness and that certainly came across today.

The Reds won a lot of their aerial duels and were convincing in their tackles and challenges across the pitch, showing a real togetherness amongst the players who were all fighting for each other out on that pitch, which is crucial if they want to get out of the position they are in.

Unbeaten run in the league continues.

Not only was it Crawley’s first home league win of the season, but it also continued their unbeaten run in the league since Blackwell arrived. It started with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere Rovers before a 0-1 win on the road against Oldham Athletic.

Something which Blackwell has reiterated in a number of interviews is full focus on the league, and that focus has proven itself in the results and now it’s all about keeping that run going and building momentum.

Recent findings suggest that the Reds looked very well organised and structured both in and out of position, rarely being caught out in the transition. Blackwell’s teams over the years have been known for being disciplined and cohesive, and that is starting to show in this Crawley side who defended very resolutely in today’s games.

Particularly with the way Crawley have played under Blackwell, they won’t dominate large proportions of the games and today was a prime example.

Both teams had different spells of pressure and dominance throughout the game, with Crawley being the ones to capitalise with two early goals at the start of each half.

#72238. Breaking: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Breaking: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3264 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • In a recent development, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

In a recent development, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

In a recent development, what a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

In a recent development, to say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

According to recent reports, and although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

In a recent development, it promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

In a recent development, could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

In a recent development, gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

Industry observers note that he seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

It has been revealed that he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

According to recent reports, alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Sources indicate that here’s what he stated immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

According to recent reports, he claims: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who stated he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

Industry observers note that hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Recent findings suggest that alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

Industry observers note that pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

Recent findings suggest that 18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a significant opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car organization makes sense, despite what I stated earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

Recent findings suggest that the Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

I’m as substantial a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

Industry observers note that “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

Recent findings suggest that “What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

Sources indicate that russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

It has been revealed that however, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Sources indicate that perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.
