Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

📅 06 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 33 min read (6607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~33 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.
  • The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead.
  • Industry observers note that others might have crumbled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Industry observers note that others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Recent findings suggest that morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

Industry observers note that this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

According to recent reports, in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be remarked that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a substantial summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

According to recent reports, “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Recent findings suggest that arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

Sources indicate that in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

Sources indicate that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Sources indicate that ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

Sources indicate that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher indicates Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Sources indicate that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

In a recent development, “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We demonstrated our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

Sources indicate that “He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

Arsenal do not play at home again until after the international break.

Sources indicate that the final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

In a recent development, pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

Madueke is brought on late for Saka.

There will be four added minutes.

That is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

In a recent development, chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

According to recent reports, arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

It has been revealed that england team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a major club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

It has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

Estevao is brought on for Chelsea in place of Neto.

Pedro wins a corner off Gabriel out on the left in front of the travelling Chelsea fans. Gusto’s delivery to the back post is caught at the second attempt by Raya.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Sources indicate that palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

In a recent development, gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

Sources indicate that the momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

In a recent development, tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

Industry observers note that that’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

According to recent reports, for the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Sources indicate that arsenal just scored the same goal they scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield. Tzolis into Odegaard, low and fast.

As it stands, Manchester City will be the only team with a 100% record after three games.

It has been revealed that it is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

It has been revealed that A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Industry observers note that the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” noted Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very important to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta mentioned. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Sources indicate that chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

“In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, substantial and small.

Sources indicate that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of significant personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

According to recent reports, arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Leeds United avenged the two cup defeats they suffered at Chelsea’s hands with a stunning 4-1 victory over their old rivals at Stamford Bridge.

Having been edged out by the Blues at the semi-final stage of the FA Cup in April, Leeds were subjected to a 6-3 Carabao Cup mauling by Xabi Alonso’s men in September.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

On this occasion, however, it was Daniel Farke’s men inflicting the damage. Emmanuel Emegha fired the hosts ahead, but Noah Okafor goals either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and a late Brenden Aaronson finish gave Leeds a Premier League win that will go down in the history books.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea sought to assume authority from the get-go, with Cole Palmer driving at the heart of the Leeds midfield inside the opening minute. The hosts may have been straight on the offensive, but Leeds soon made it clear they would not be content with one-way traffic.

Jayden Bogle and Sean Longstaff both made headway down the right-hand side, sending in crosses that were not capitalised upon.

Recent findings suggest that the opening exchanges played out in a fast and furious manner, with robust challenges stoking the fires of a historic rivalry. Chelsea had the early edge, although referee Michael Oliver had no interest in appeals for a penalty when Tarik Muharemovic challenged Emmanuel Emegha inside the box.

Leeds handled Chelsea’s ventures forward well, mostly limiting the Blues to speculative efforts. Josh Acheamping, Morgan Rogers and Estevao all pulled the trigger from distance, yet little was asked of James Trafford between the Leeds sticks.

Industry observers note that at the other end, Leeds continued to make inroads on the right. James Justin whipped a cross over for Calvert-Lewin, who struggled to generate power but did hit the crossbar with his looped header.

It has been revealed that leeds’ focus soon shifted to the left, where Gudmundsson started to flex his attacking muscles. He made an incisive dart into the box and went to ground under close attention from Estevao, although the referee paid no attention to penalty appeals.

Leeds’ left wing-back then picked out Calvert-Lewin and saw the England international force a strong hand from Emiliano Martinez with a headed effort.

Recent findings suggest that the visitors looked to be moving through the gears but just as the tide was turning, Chelsea drew first blood. Justin and Nico Elvedi both failed to stop the advancement of Rogers, who fed Emegha and saw the frontman beat Trafford at his near post with a blasted finish.

Leeds bit back almost immediately, levelling proceedings within three minutes of the opener. Calvert-Lewin contested a long ball with Wesley Fofana before picking up the scraps and releasing Okafor, who jinked his way into space and rifled across Martinez.

With the wind behind their sails, Leeds came close to overturning the deficit via their equaliser’s creator. Calvert-Lewin met a Muharemovic cross and his deft flick came agonisingly close to finding the bottom corner.

Farke’s men continued applying pressure in the closing stages of the first half and Ao Tanaka was unfortunate to see a rasping rocket of a shot deflected before it could cause Martinez any trouble.

Gudmundsson then danced his way into an opportunity before poking harmlessly wide of Martinez’s right-hand post.

The next chance fell to Tanaka, who pushed the ball out of his feet but could only force a straightforward save with a shot straight down Martinez’s throat.

Sources indicate that leeds did have the ball in the back of the net on the stroke of half-time, although Justin was clearly offside before he delivered for Muharemovic to finish. When the half-time whistle did blow, it was Leeds firmly in the driving seat.

According to recent reports, the second half started as the first ended, with Leeds in the ascendency. There were early appeals for a penalty when Calvert-Lewin tangled with Martinez, but Oliver was again dismissive of protests.

Tanaka then stretched to get on the end of a cross from deep, steering just off target as pressure piled on Chelsea.

According to recent reports, having seen their protests ignored mere minutes earlier, Leeds saw Oliver point to the spot when Rogers was judged to have handled a Muharemovic shot. After a lengthy VAR check, the decision was stuck by and Calvert-Lewin buried the spot-kick.

Chelsea responded by putting their front foot forward and Rogers forced Trafford down to his left with a low drive from distance.

According to recent reports, however, it was Leeds who struck next and sent the the travelling supporters into a frenzy. After Chelsea failed to clear their lines after a long throw, Ethan Ampadu’s deflected cross was hammered home by Okafor in emphatic fashion.

It has been revealed that somewhat predictably, Chelsea surged back into the driving seat as they looked for a way back into a game getting away from them. Much to the frustration of the home supporters, their spell of control yielded little more than occasional half-chances.

There were sharp inhales of breath when Rogers arrowed a free-kick goalwards from a tight angle, but it dipped over the crossbar with Trafford at full stretch.

Many of Chelsea’s supporters were already heading out to beat the traffic when Aaronson capped an astonishing afternoon, wriggling through a creaking defence before steering a fourth past Martinez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan defender Strahinja Pavlovic has spoken about potentially retiring alongside Diego Moreira in the future, after a fresh revelation.

According to recent reports, it’s clear that, since he’s arrived, Moreira has had a huge impact on the dressing room. In terms of quality, Mark van Bommel called him ‘crazy’, but compared him to Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, then, Koni De Winter repeated similar sentiments today, saying that he may be a little crazy, but he was a good character to be around and a great footballer and Milan fans can see this, too. The Belgian is already making the €50 million paid for him look like a bargain and he has plenty of room left for growth.

Speaking to SS Calcio, Pavlovic looked at his relationship with Moreira, the help from Massimiliano Allegri last season and who gave him the most difficult game in his career, as MilanPress relayed.

“Working with Allegri was beneficial for me. It’s under his guidance that I’ve made the most progress since arriving in Italy. As a central defender, I possess good speed, strength, and skill with the ball.

In a recent development, “I can pass the ball forward and score goals, but tactical skills have always been a weakness of mine. I only learned the basics when I joined the first team at Partizan. Given the way Italians view football, I was a bit behind the times, as their players begin to grasp certain concepts from a very young age.”.

It has been revealed that “Physically, the toughest challenge was undoubtedly against Romelu Lukaku. But also Marcus Thuram: he’s strong, quick, and very skilled with the ball at his feet. With Lautaro, however, you have to be very careful inside the penalty area: if you don’t stay close to him, he’ll score.

“You can’t leave him any space.”.

The bond that unites Moreira and Pavlovic….

Sources indicate that “I didn’t even know he was Almami’s son [a former Partizan player]. He’s a fantastic guy, really smart. He knows a few bits of Serbian. I met his father during a training session. We talked about Partizan, of course. It was really nice to see him; I remember him from his time at Partizan.”.

The possibility of joining Partizan at the end of his career….

“I often joke with Moreira, telling him that, at the end of our careers, we should play at least one season at Partizan. I point out that I’m three years older than him, so he’ll have to make a small sacrifice so we can get back together. He’s a truly great guy.

Sources indicate that “There’s a fantastic atmosphere in our group. It’s a real pleasure to be part of Milan.”.

Breaking: Man United star Bryan Mbeumo stays up late to play GTA6 on morning of his new boss's first day at work: Athletes' performances to 'plummet' for weeks as Liverpool and Arsenal players reveal their video game all-nighters

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.
  • In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt fresh Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

In a recent development, in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The newly introduced boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the strategy.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

Sources indicate that 'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

In a recent development, it’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor revealed that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the upcoming GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

He told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor declared that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was released.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

Industry observers note that 🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the strategy.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

It has been revealed that 'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a major one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' mentioned Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

Industry observers note that new York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall said. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the problem as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after substantial games.

Those concerns appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis mentioned it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

"Because there's a lot of ability in the group.

"We went 1-0 down, we didn't panic, we equalised. We went 2-1 down, we didn't panic. The two goals were great for us.”.

Earmarking special praise for James Collins following his debut from the bench, he added: “It was brilliant from James Collins for the first one to tee up JT and it was a brilliant overhead kick.

"And again, the delivery from Gottsy (Robbie Gotts) and the experience of Colo to take two of their defenders under the ball to free up Sean was excellent.”.

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

Industry observers note that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

It has been revealed that “Brilliant technique,” stated David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

In a recent development, benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

Recent findings suggest that united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Recent findings suggest that yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

It has been revealed that “We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

Sources indicate that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

Industry observers note that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

According to recent reports, “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes remarked. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

In a recent development, they did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

In a recent development, it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

Recent findings suggest that I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Recent findings suggest that george finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

In a recent development, good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having mentioned that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.
